summary.text: Saint Alypius was a monk, priest, and iconographer of the Kiev Caves. The ecclesiastical life remembers his icon painting, charity, and accounts of miraculous help.

blocks.text: He entered the Kiev Caves monastic community and learned icon painting from Greek artists working there in 1083. He received monastic tonsure and later became a hieromonk, meaning a monk ordained as a priest.
blocks.reason: Concise source-bound biography; the modern ecclesiastical life is paraphrased rather than substantially reproduced. Historical uncertainty and hagiographic accounts retain their source attribution.

blocks.text: The life presents him repairing church icons without charging. Payments were divided among supplies, alms, and his needs. It also recounts a commission concealed from him by two monks; the subsequent appearance of completed icons belongs to its miracle narrative.

blocks.text: In its account of his final illness, an angel completes an unfinished icon. Saint Alypius dies in 1114 and is buried in the Near Caves. The source describes repose, not martyrdom.

blocks.text: His legacy is chiefly iconography. The source associates him with the Sven-Caves icon and remembers him among the Kiev Caves Saints. August 17 is his individual feast; September 28 and a Lenten synaxis provide additional commemorations.
